catalog: Acme TechGRC control automation use cases
note: Fictional Acme policy values and candidate framework mappings. Mappings require review against the authoritative text by the control steward and the assessor.

usecases.name: Leaver access removal
usecases.objective: Access for terminated workers is removed from the identity provider and from cloud-native credentials within the Acme SLA.
usecases.risk: A former worker, or anyone holding their credential, keeps access to production data after termination.
usecases.automation: Fully automated test with human triage of failures
usecases.frequency: Daily, plus on each HR termination event
usecases.population: Workers whose HR status is terminated with an effective time at or before the as-of time

sources.record: Worker status and termination effective time with UTC offset
Account enabled state, disable time and worker ID
IAM credential report: access_key_1_active, access_key_1_last_used_date, password_enabled
sources.api: aws iam generate-credential-report, aws iam get-credential-report

sources.record: Entra ID user accountEnabled and on-premises sync state; storage account shared keys are tracked separately
User-managed service account keys created for the worker

logic: Correlate each terminated worker to identity-provider accounts by worker ID and to cloud credentials by owner tag.
FAIL when an account is still enabled, was disabled later than the SLA, or a cloud-native credential remains active.
UNKNOWN when nothing correlates to the worker or a disable time is missing.
NOT_APPLICABLE when the termination is effective after the as-of time.
itgc_dependencies: Change management over the use-case code and parameters
Restricted write access to the HR-to-GRC integration mapping
usecases.remediation: Disable the account and revoke or delete each active credential, then find why the deprovisioning event did not reach that system.
usecases.retest: Re-run on the affected worker from an independent collector identity and confirm no credential activity after the removal time.
usecases.limitations: Correlation depends on worker IDs and owner tags. Shared or untagged credentials need a separate ownership control.

usecases.name: Privileged MFA enforcement
usecases.objective: Every enabled account in a cloud administrator group is covered by an enforcing MFA policy and holds a strong method.
usecases.risk: A stolen password alone grants administrative control of a cloud environment.
usecases.population: Enabled identity-provider accounts in the AWS, Azure and GCP administrator groups

sources.record: Group membership, MFA policy assignment result and registered methods
IAM Identity Center permission-set assignments that map groups to accounts
Conditional Access policies and authentication method registration
Organization IAM bindings for administrator groups

logic: Select enabled accounts holding at least one privileged group.
FAIL when no enforcing MFA policy applies, or only weak methods are registered.
Break-glass accounts need a valid, independently approved exclusion. Otherwise FAIL.
UNKNOWN when policy assignment or methods were not collected.
itgc_dependencies: Change management over the privileged group list in the parameters
usecases.remediation: Bring the account under the enforcing policy and register a strong method, or remove the privileged group.
usecases.retest: Re-collect policy assignment and methods for the account and confirm a strong-method sign-in is required.
usecases.limitations: Registration and policy assignment are inputs. The test does not replay a sign-in.

usecases.name: Production change approval
usecases.objective: Each production deployment traces to a merged change approved by someone other than the author at the deployed commit.
usecases.risk: Unreviewed or self-approved code reaches production.
usecases.automation: Fully automated test over the full deployment population
usecases.population: Deployments to production in the period across AWS, Azure and GCP pipelines

sources.record: Deployment ID, environment, commit SHA, deployer and time
Pull requests associated with a commit, reviews with state and commit_id
Pull request reviewers and votes; branch policy allowing requestors to approve their own changes
sources.api: Azure DevOps Git pull requests REST API

sources.record: Emergency change records with retrospective approval

logic: Trace each production deployment's commit SHA to a merged pull request.
FAIL when there is no approval, the only approval is the author's, or the approval predates the final commit.
A deployment without a pull request passes only with an emergency change approved by someone else within the window.
UNKNOWN when the deployment record lacks a commit SHA.
itgc_dependencies: Repository branch protection is itself monitored under the configuration baseline
usecases.remediation: Obtain retrospective review of the deployed change, and enforce branch protection that blocks self-approval and stale approval.
usecases.retest: Test the next deployments from the same repository and confirm the branch policy setting through its API.
usecases.limitations: Proves traceability and independent approval. It does not judge review quality or test adequacy.

usecases.name: Audit log coverage and delivery
usecases.objective: Each cloud scope exports audit logs, and a canary event reaches the monitored destination within the SLO.
usecases.risk: Security-relevant activity is not recorded, or is recorded but never reaches the people who monitor it.
usecases.automation: Fully automated configuration test plus an injected canary event
usecases.population: Declared AWS accounts, Azure subscriptions and GCP projects

sources.record: Trail IsMultiRegionTrail and IsLogging
sources.api: aws cloudtrail describe-trails, aws cloudtrail get-trail-status

sources.record: Subscription diagnostic settings and enabled log categories
Log sinks and IAM policy auditConfigs for Data Access logs
sources.api: gcloud logging sinks list, gcloud projects get-iam-policy

sources.record: Canary event receipt time

logic: Apply the provider-specific configuration predicate.
For GCP projects hosting ePHI, require DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE audit logs for Cloud Storage.
Emit a canary event and FAIL when it does not arrive, or arrives after the SLO.
UNKNOWN when configuration or canary results were not collected.
itgc_dependencies: Change management over SIEM ingestion filters
Monitoring of the canary job itself
usecases.remediation: Restore the export configuration or the delivery path, then backfill missing events where the source retains them.
usecases.retest: Emit a new canary and reconcile a full hour of source events against the destination.
usecases.limitations: A canary proves one path for one event type. It does not show that every event type survives ingestion filters. See DF-01.

usecases.name: ePHI encryption with customer-managed keys
usecases.objective: Datastores tagged as holding ePHI are encrypted with an enabled customer-managed key that rotates within the Acme limit.
usecases.risk: ePHI is protected only by provider-managed keys that Acme cannot revoke, or by keys that never rotate.
usecases.population: All declared datastores. Only those tagged ephi are in scope

sources.record: Bucket or database encryption settings, KMS KeyManager, KeyState and rotation
sources.api: aws s3api get-bucket-encryption, aws rds describe-db-instances, aws kms describe-key, aws kms get-key-rotation-status

sources.record: Storage or database encryption keySource and Key Vault key rotation policy
sources.api: az storage account show, az keyvault key rotation-policy show

sources.record: Default KMS key name and CryptoKey rotationPeriod
sources.api: Cloud Storage buckets.get, gcloud kms keys describe

logic: NOT_APPLICABLE unless the reviewed classification includes the ephi tag.
FAIL when encryption is off, the key is provider-managed, the key is not enabled, or rotation exceeds the limit.
UNKNOWN when encryption, key metadata or rotation was not collected.
itgc_dependencies: Classification tags are reviewed by the data owner
usecases.remediation: Re-encrypt or migrate to a customer-managed key, and set rotation through infrastructure as code.
usecases.retest: Re-collect encryption and key metadata from an independent identity.
usecases.limitations: Customer-managed keys are a fictional Acme policy choice, not HIPAA text. HIPAA encryption at rest is an addressable specification.

usecases.name: Backup coverage and restore evidence
usecases.objective: Tier 1 datastores have a recent recovery point and a recent restore exercise with integrity verified within the RTO.
usecases.risk: Backups exist on paper but cannot restore the service within the committed objectives.
usecases.automation: Automated test over backup exports and the restore register
usecases.frequency: Daily for recovery points, quarterly for restore exercises

sources.record: Protected resources, recovery points and restore jobs
sources.api: aws backup list-protected-resources, aws backup list-recovery-points-by-resource, aws backup list-restore-jobs

sources.record: Backup items and recovery points
sources.api: az backup item list, az backup recoverypoint list

sources.record: Backup and DR backup plans or Cloud SQL backups
Exercise time, elapsed hours and integrity verification

logic: NOT_APPLICABLE unless the datastore is tier 1.
FAIL when there is no backup plan, the recovery point is older than the RPO, or there is no recent restore with integrity verified within the RTO.
UNKNOWN when the recovery point time or restore duration is missing.
itgc_dependencies: The restore register is complete and controlled
usecases.remediation: Assign the datastore to a backup plan, fix the failing job, or schedule and record a representative restore.
usecases.retest: Confirm a new recovery point and a restore record with integrity evidence.
usecases.limitations: A single restore of one datastore does not prove recovery of the whole service.

usecases.name: Vulnerability remediation within SLA
usecases.objective: Scanned compute assets have no open critical or high finding older than the Acme SLA.
usecases.risk: Known exploitable weaknesses stay open past the agreed window, or unscanned assets look clean.
usecases.automation: Fully automated test with scan-coverage gating
usecases.population: Declared compute assets across AWS, Azure and GCP

sources.record: Inspector findings with severity, status and first observed time
Defender for Cloud assessments in the securityresources table
Security Command Center vulnerability findings

logic: UNKNOWN when the asset was not scanned within the window, because a missing scan looks like a clean result.
FAIL for each open critical or high finding older than its SLA, even when the scan is stale.
itgc_dependencies: SLA values are approved by management
Scanner coverage is reconciled to the asset inventory
usecases.remediation: Patch or rebuild from a fixed image, or record a time-bound exception.
usecases.retest: Rescan the asset and every asset built from the same image.
usecases.limitations: The SLA values are fictional Acme policy values, not framework requirements.

usecases.name: Privileged access review completeness
usecases.objective: Quarterly privileged access reviews cover the full group, are decided by someone other than the account holder, and revocations take effect.
usecases.risk: A review is marked complete while accounts were left out, self-approved, or never actually removed.
usecases.automation: Hybrid: human review decisions, automated completeness and follow-through test
usecases.population: Q3 2026 review campaigns for each privileged group

sources.record: Campaign items, reviewers, decisions and completion time
sources.api: Microsoft Graph /identityGovernance/accessReviews/definitions, or the review tool export

sources.record: Group membership snapshot at campaign start and current membership

logic: Reconcile campaign items to the membership snapshot taken at campaign start.
FAIL when members are missing from the review, items are undecided or self-reviewed, revocations did not take effect, or the campaign finished late.
UNKNOWN when no membership snapshot exists.
itgc_dependencies: Snapshot job runs at campaign start and is retained
usecases.remediation: Review the missing accounts, execute pending revocations and reassign self-reviewed items.
usecases.retest: Re-run against current membership and the next campaign's snapshot.
usecases.limitations: Tests completeness and follow-through. It does not judge whether each keep decision was appropriate.
